searchDocs.title: Active​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Scope.Active: boolean true until the state is left and the scope is cleaned up. A scope is never reused: entering the state again gives it a new one.

searchDocs.title: Add​
searchDocs.content: </> Scope:Add( item: T-- A function, thread, Instance, RBXScriptConnection, or a table with a Destroy or Disconnect method ) → T-- The same item, so it can be added inline Cleans item up when the state is left: functions are called, threads cancelled, Instances destroyed, connections disconnected, and tables have their Destroy (or Disconnect) method called. Items are cleaned in reverse order of adding. Adding to a scope that was already cleaned cleans the item immediately. local hitbox = machine:GetScope():Add(Hitbox.new(character))

searchDocs.title: Delay​
searchDocs.content: </> Scope:Delay( seconds: number,-- Machine time to wait, advanced by Machine:Update callback: (...any) → (),-- Called with ... ...: any ) → () → ()-- Cancels the timer Calls callback after seconds of machine time, unless the state is left first. Timers are driven by Machine:Update, so they never fire without it, and fire at the earliest on the next Update. -- Open the cancel window 0.25s into the attack machine:GetScope():Delay(0.25, function() machine.Context.CanCancel = true end)

searchDocs.title: From​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.From: string The state this transition leaves. It must match the state whose Transitions list it's in (Machine:Start checks), or be "*" for transitions in Machine.AnyTransitions.

searchDocs.title: Target​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.Target: string The name of the state to enter.

searchDocs.title: Triggers​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.Triggers: {string} The trigger names that fire this transition.

searchDocs.title: Conditions​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.Conditions: {Condition} Guards. All must return true for the transition to fire.

searchDocs.title: Effects​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.Effects: {Effect} Actions, run in order after the old state exits and before the new state enters.

searchDocs.title: Priority​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.Priority: number? How hard this transition interrupts. It only fires if Priority is at least the current state's State.Resistance. Defaults to 0. Use math.huge for transitions nothing should block, like dying.

searchDocs.title: Except​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.Except: {string}? For transitions in [Machine.AnyTransitions]: states it doesn't fire from. A state's children are excluded too.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Transition.new(params: { From: string, Target: string, Triggers: {string}, Conditions: {Condition}?, Effects: {Effect}?, Priority: number?, Except: {string}? }) → Transition

searchDocs.title: Name​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Name: string The state's name. Transitions target states by this name, so it must be unique within a machine.

searchDocs.title: Transitions​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Transitions: {Transition} The transitions that can leave this state, checked in order when a trigger is sent. Add to it with table.insert.

searchDocs.title: OnEnter​
searchDocs.content: </> State.OnEnter: Callback? Called with the machine and any event data when the machine enters this state.

searchDocs.title: OnExit​
searchDocs.content: </> State.OnExit: Callback? Called with the machine and any event data when the machine leaves this state.

searchDocs.title: OnUpdate​
searchDocs.content: </> State.OnUpdate: UpdateCallback? Called with the machine and dt on every Machine:Update while the machine is in this state (or in one of its children). Parents run before children.

searchDocs.title: Parent​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Parent: string? The name of this state's parent, for hierarchical machines. While a child is active its parents are too:Machine:Is matches them, their transitions, State.Tags and State.Resistance apply, and they're only exited when a transition leaves them. local combat = Flux.State.new("Combat") local light = Flux.State.new("Light") light.Parent = "Combat"

searchDocs.title: Initial​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Initial: string? The child entered automatically when this state is entered, so a transition can target a parent.

searchDocs.title: Duration​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Duration: number? Seconds of machine time after which the machine moves to State.Next on its own. Driven by Machine:Update. The move ignores Conditions and [State.Resistance]: it's the state ending, not an interrupt. windup.Duration = 0.15 windup.Next = "Active"

searchDocs.title: Next​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Next: string? The state entered when State.Duration runs out. Required when Duration is set.

searchDocs.title: Resistance​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Resistance: Resistance? The minimum Transition.Priority needed to leave this state, or a function returning it. Defaults to the nearest parent's Resistance, or 0. A function is re-evaluated on every Send, which makes cancel windows easy: -- Uncancellable for the first 0.25s, then anything goes heavy.Resistance = function(machine) return if machine:GetTimeInState() < 0.25 then 10 else 0 end Timeouts (State.Duration), Machine:ForceState and Machine:Stop ignore it.

searchDocs.title: Tags​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Tags: {[string]: any}? Values that describe the state, read with Machine:HasTag and Machine:GetTag. A child's tag overrides its parent's. dodge.Tags = { Invulnerable = true, CanMove = false }

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> State.new( name: string-- The state's name, unique within its machine ) → State

searchDocs.title: Trigger​
searchDocs.content: </> State:Trigger( trigger: string, machine: Machine, ...: any-- Event data, passed to each Condition ) → Transition?-- The first transition listening for trigger whose Conditions all pass Finds the transition in this state's own Transitions that a trigger would fire, without running it. It doesn't look at parents, the machine's AnyTransitions or State.Resistance; use Machine:CanSend for that.

searchDocs.title: Driving the machine with Update​
searchDocs.content: Anything time-based (durations, delays, input buffer windows, time in state) uses machine time, which only moves when you call Update:  RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt) fighter:Update(dt) end)   Each Update advances machine.Clock by dt, then, in order:  fires due Scope:Delay timersmoves on from states whose Duration ran outcalls each active state's OnUpdate(machine, dt), parents firstretries buffered triggers  Because time only comes from Update, a machine is deterministic: the same dts and triggers always give the same result, which makes combat code easy to test and to reproduce on the server.

searchDocs.title: Timed states​
searchDocs.content: Attacks are usually phases. Give a state a Duration and a Next, and it moves on by itself:  local windup = Flux.State.new("Windup") windup.Duration = 0.15 windup.Next = "Swing" local swing = Flux.State.new("Swing") swing.Duration = 0.1 swing.Next = "Recovery"   A timeout ignores Conditions and Resistance: it's the state ending, not something interrupting it.  For anything time-dependent, use GetTimeInState in a Condition:  Conditions = { function(machine) return machine:GetTimeInState() >= 0.2 -- combo window opens 0.2s in end, }

searchDocs.title: Cleaning up with scopes​
searchDocs.content: Combat states create things: hitboxes, sounds, animation connections, timers. When the state is interrupted, all of it has to go. Every stay in a state has a Scope, and everything added to it is cleaned up when the state is left, however it's left:  swing.OnEnter = function(machine) local scope = machine:GetScope() local hitbox = scope:Add(Hitbox.new(character)) -- hitbox:Destroy() on exit scope:Add(hitbox.Touched:Connect(onHit)) -- disconnected on exit scope:Add(function() -- called on exit track:Stop() end) scope:Delay(0.05, function() -- never fires if the swing is interrupted first hitbox:Enable() end) end   Add takes functions, threads, Instances, connections, and tables with a Destroy or Disconnect method. Inside OnEnter, OnExit, OnUpdate and Delay callbacks, machine:GetScope() is the scope of the state the callback belongs to.  Don't yield in callbacks If a callback yields (task.wait()), the transition isn't finished until it resumes, and every trigger sent in the meantime is queued, so inputs pile up and then fire all at once. Use scope:Delay instead. Set CatchYields = true in the machine's details (it's on in DebugMode) to turn an accidental yield into an error.

searchDocs.title: Interrupts from any state​
searchDocs.content: Getting hit, stunned or killed can happen in almost every state. Instead of adding the same transition to each one, put it in machine.AnyTransitions:  table.insert(fighter.AnyTransitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "*", Target = "Stunned", Triggers = { "Stun" }, Except = { "Dead" }, }))   They're checked after the current state's own transitions (and its parents'), so a state can handle a trigger its own way. For example, Blocking can turn Hit into BlockStun.

searchDocs.title: Priority and Resistance​
searchDocs.content: Not everything can interrupt everything. A transition's Priority must be at least the current state's Resistance to fire (both default to 0):  heavy.Resistance = 5 -- armored: light hits don't interrupt Flux.Transition.new({ From = "*", Target = "HitReact", Triggers = { "Hit" }, Priority = 1 }) Flux.Transition.new({ From = "*", Target = "Staggered", Triggers = { "Stagger" }, Priority = 10 }) Flux.Transition.new({ From = "*", Target = "Dead", Triggers = { "Die" }, Priority = math.huge })   Resistance can be a function, re-evaluated on every trigger, which makes cancel windows one line:  -- Can't be cancelled for the first 0.25s, then anything goes heavy.Resistance = function(machine) return if machine:GetTimeInState() < 0.25 then 10 else 0 end

searchDocs.title: Input buffering​
searchDocs.content: Players press attack slightly before the current attack ends. With Send, that press is lost. WithBuffer, it's kept for a window and retried after every transition and every Update:  fighter:Buffer("Attack", 0.2) -- fires now if it can, otherwise within the next 0.2s if it becomes possible   Buffering a trigger that's already buffered replaces it, so mashing buffers one press. ClearBuffer drops them, and Stop clears the buffer.

searchDocs.title: Hierarchical states​
searchDocs.content: Set a state's Parent to group states. While a child is active, its parents are too:  local attacking = Flux.State.new("Attacking") attacking.Initial = "Light1" -- targeting Attacking enters Light1 attacking.Tags = { CanMove = false } local light1 = Flux.State.new("Light1") light1.Parent = "Attacking" local light2 = Flux.State.new("Light2") light2.Parent = "Attacking"   A parent's transitions, Tags and Resistance apply to its children (a child's own win).Moving between children of the same parent doesn't exit the parent, so its scope survives the whole combo.machine:Is("Attacking") is true in Light1 and Light2.machine.Current is the innermost active state.

searchDocs.title: Tags​
searchDocs.content: Instead of asking "is the fighter in Dodge, or Roll, or Parry?", ask what the state means:  dodge.Tags = { Invulnerable = true, CanMove = false } if not target:HasTag("Invulnerable") then target:Send("Hit", damage) end

searchDocs.title: Asking before sending​
searchDocs.content: CanSend checks a trigger without firing it, for UI and AI. Rejected fires whenever a Send doesn't transition. Both give a reason: "NoTransition", "Conditions", "Resisted" or "Inactive".  local canDodge, reason = fighter:CanSend("Dodge") fighter.Rejected:Connect(function(trigger, reason) print(trigger, "rejected:", reason) -- "Parry rejected: Resisted" end)   CanSend runs the Conditions, so keep them free of side effects.

searchDocs.title: History​
searchDocs.content: machine.Previous is the state before the last transition, and GetHistory() returns the last few state names, oldest first (8 by default, set with HistorySize).

searchDocs.title: Networking​
searchDocs.content: Snapshot() returns { State, Time } as plain data, and ForceState(name, elapsed) moves straight to a state with the given time already elapsed, skipping Conditions, Effects and Resistance. Together they let a server correct a client:  -- Server remote:FireClient(player, fighter:Snapshot()) -- Client remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(snapshot) if snapshot.State and not fighter:Is(snapshot.State) then fighter:ForceState(snapshot.State, snapshot.Time) end end)   Context isn't part of the snapshot; replicate the values you need yourself.

searchDocs.title: Changing transitions at runtime​
searchDocs.content: Inserting a transition or state after Start is picked up automatically. After replacing or removing one, or changing a transition's Triggers, call machine:Refresh().

searchDocs.title: Current​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.Current: State? The state the machine is in, or nil when it isn't running. In a hierarchical machine this is the innermost active state; use Machine:Is to also match its parents.

searchDocs.title: Previous​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.Previous: State? The state the machine was in before the last transition, or nil right after Machine:Start.

searchDocs.title: Active​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.Active: boolean Whether the machine is running: true between Machine:Start and Machine:Stop.

searchDocs.title: Context​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine.Context: C A table shared by every callback, for data like health, ammo or a target. It's the same table passed asContext in Flux.Details, or an empty table if none was passed.

searchDocs.title: Clock​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.Clock: number Machine time in seconds: the sum of every dt passed to Machine:Update. State.Duration, Scope:Delay, Machine:Buffer windows and Machine:GetTimeInState all use it.

searchDocs.title: AnyTransitions​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine.AnyTransitions: {Transition} Transitions that can fire from any state, for interrupts like getting stunned or dying. They're checked after the current state's own transitions and its parents', so a state can handle a trigger its own way. Their From must be "*", and their Except lists states they don't fire from. table.insert(fighter.AnyTransitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "*", Target = "Dead", Triggers = { "Die" }, Priority = math.huge, Except = { "Dead" }, }))

searchDocs.title: ID​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.ID: any The id passed to Flux.new. Used in error messages.

searchDocs.title: Default​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.Default: string The name of the state entered by Machine:Start.

searchDocs.title: StateChanged​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.StateChanged: Signal Fires with (newState, oldState, ...) whenever Machine.Current changes: after a state's OnEnter runs, and after OnExit when the machine stops. ... is the event data passed to Machine:Send. newState is nil on Machine:Stop, and oldState is nil on Machine:Start; neither has event data. A Machine:Send made from a handler is queued like one made from any other callback. Handlers run on their own thread. If a handler yields, the machine may have moved on by the time it resumes, so use the newState argument rather than reading Machine.Current after a yield. local connection = machine.StateChanged:Connect(function(newState, oldState, ...) print(oldState and oldState.Name, "->", newState and newState.Name, ...) end) connection:Disconnect()

searchDocs.title: Rejected​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Machine.Rejected: Signal Fires with (trigger, reason, ...) when a Machine:Send doesn't transition. reason is a Flux.RejectReason. Triggers retried by Machine:Buffer don't fire it. fighter.Rejected:Connect(function(trigger, reason) warn(`{trigger} rejected: {reason}`) --> Parry rejected: Resisted end)

searchDocs.title: Send​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Send( trigger: string,-- The trigger name ...: any-- Event data, passed after the machine to the Conditions, the old state's OnExit, the Effects and the new state's OnEnter ) → boolean-- true if the machine transitioned Sends a trigger. The machine looks for a transition listening for trigger in the current state's Transitions (in the order they were inserted), then in each parent's, then in Machine.AnyTransitions. The first one whose Priority meets the current State.Resistance and whose Conditions all pass fires. If none does, nothing happens, Machine.Rejected fires, and Send returns false. A Send made from inside a callback is queued and runs after the current transition has fully finished, so it returns false. Errors thrown by callbacks are rethrown from Send. If a callback yields (for example with task.wait()), the transition isn't finished until it resumes, so every Send in the meantime is queued. That's rarely what you want in combat: use Scope:Delay to wait instead. Set CatchYields (or DebugMode) in Flux.Details to turn a yield into an error, which stops the callback where it yielded. player:Send("Hit", 25, "Zombie")

searchDocs.title: Buffer​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Buffer( trigger: string, window: number,-- How long to keep retrying, in machine time ...: any-- Event data, passed as with Machine:Send ) → boolean-- true if it transitioned right away Like Machine:Send, but if the trigger can't fire now it's kept for window seconds and retried after every transition and every Machine:Update, until it fires or expires. For input buffering: an attack pressed just before the current one ends still comes out. Buffering a trigger that's already buffered replaces it, so mashing a button buffers one press. UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input) if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then fighter:Buffer("Attack", 0.2) end end)

searchDocs.title: ClearBuffer​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:ClearBuffer( trigger: string?-- Only clear this trigger. Clears everything when omitted. ) → () Drops buffered triggers. Machine:Stop clears the buffer too.

searchDocs.title: CanSend​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:CanSend( trigger: string, ...: any-- Event data, passed to the Conditions ) → ( boolean,-- Whether Machine:Send would transition right now RejectReason?-- Why not, when it wouldn't ) Checks a trigger without sending it, for UI and AI ("can I dodge right now?"). It runs the Conditions, so keep them free of side effects. local canDodge, reason = fighter:CanSend("Dodge")

searchDocs.title: Update​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Update( dt: number-- Seconds since the last Update ) → () Advances machine time by dt, then, in order: fires due Scope:Delay timers, moves on from states whose State.Duration ran out, calls each active state's State.OnUpdate, and retries buffered triggers. Call it every frame: RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt) fighter:Update(dt) end) Nothing time-based happens without it. Machines that don't use time don't need it.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Can't Update during a transition."	Called from inside a callback

searchDocs.title: Start​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Start() → () Enters the default state (and its parents, and its State.Initial children). Calling it on a running machine exits the current state and starts over. Before entering anything, Start checks the machine's setup, so typos fail at setup instead of mid-game: state names are unique, the default state exists, every transition's Target names one of the machine's states and its From matches the state it's in, and every Parent, Initial, Next and Except names a real state.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Default State not Defined."	The default state isn't one of the machine's states "... has a Transition to ..., which Doesn't Exist."	A transition targets a state the machine doesn't have "Can't Start during a transition."	Called from inside a callback

searchDocs.title: Stop​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Stop() → () Exits the current state (and its parents) and stops the machine, cleaning up every Scope and clearing buffered triggers. Triggers sent while stopped are ignored. Call Machine:Start to run it again. Called from inside a callback, it waits until the current transition finishes, then discards any queued triggers.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Destroy() → () Stops the machine and releases its states and details. Like Machine:Stop, it waits for the current transition to finish when called from inside a callback.

searchDocs.title: ForceState​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:ForceState( name: string,-- The state to move to elapsed: number?-- How long the machine has already been in it. Defaults to 0. ) → () Moves straight to a state, skipping Conditions, Effects and State.Resistance (exits and enters still run). If the machine is already in that state, only its time is changed. For applying a server's Machine:Snapshot on a client, or resetting a fighter at round start. Scope:Delay timers aren't shifted by elapsed. -- Client: snap to the server's state when prediction was wrong remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(snapshot) if snapshot.State and not fighter:Is(snapshot.State) then fighter:ForceState(snapshot.State, snapshot.Time) end end)

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Isn't Active."	The machine isn't running "Can't ForceState during a transition."	Called from inside a callback

searchDocs.title: Snapshot​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Snapshot() → Snapshot The current state's name and how long the machine has been in it, as plain data to send to clients. Apply it with Machine:ForceState. Machine.Context isn't included.

searchDocs.title: Is​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Is(name: string) → boolean-- Whether the machine is in name, or in a child of it if fighter:Is("Attacking") then -- true in Attacking's children too

searchDocs.title: IsAny​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:IsAny(names: {string}) → boolean-- Whether Machine:Is is true for any of names

searchDocs.title: GetTag​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:GetTag(tag: string) → any-- The tag's value in the innermost active state that sets it, or nil Reads State.Tags. A child's value overrides its parent's.

searchDocs.title: HasTag​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:HasTag(tag: string) → boolean-- Whether Machine:GetTag is truthy Lets damage, movement and UI code ask about the state instead of checking state names: if not target:HasTag("Invulnerable") then target:Send("Hit", damage) end

searchDocs.title: GetScope​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:GetScope( name: string?-- An active state. Defaults to the state whose callback is running, or Machine.Current. ) → Scope The Scope for the current stay in a state: everything added to it is cleaned up when the machine leaves that state. Inside OnEnter, OnExit, OnUpdate and Scope:Delay callbacks, machine:GetScope() is the scope of the state the callback belongs to.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"... isn't active."	The state isn't active (for example, from inside an Effect, between states)

searchDocs.title: GetTimeInState​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:GetTimeInState( name: string?-- An active state. Defaults to Machine.Current. ) → number-- Machine time since the state was entered, or 0 if it isn't active -- A Condition: only cancel into a dodge after the attack's first 0.2s function(machine) return machine:GetTimeInState() >= 0.2 end

searchDocs.title: GetHistory​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:GetHistory() → {string}-- State names, oldest first, ending with Machine.Current The names of the last states the machine was in. Keeps Flux.Details HistorySize entries (8 by default). Cleared by Machine:Start. Returns a new table each call. -- Back to whatever stance we were in before getting hit local history = fighter:GetHistory() local before = history[#history - 1]

searchDocs.title: Refresh​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:Refresh() → () Rebuilds the machine's lookup tables. Inserting transitions or states after Machine:Start is picked up automatically; call this after replacing or removing them, or after changing a transition's Triggers.

searchDocs.title: GetStates​
searchDocs.content: </> Machine:GetStates() → {State}?-- The machine's states, or nil if it has none or was destroyed

searchDocs.title: Installation​
searchDocs.content: With Wally, add Flux to your wally.toml:  [dependencies] Flux = "3b-6/flux@0.1.0"   Then run wally install and require it:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Flux = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Flux)   Flux has no dependencies and works anywhere Luau runs: on the client, on the server, and in Lune.

searchDocs.title: Quick start​
searchDocs.content: A character that can idle, walk and jump:  --!strict local Flux = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Flux) -- 1. Create the states local idle = Flux.State.new("Idle") local walk = Flux.State.new("Walk") local jump = Flux.State.new("Jump") idle.OnEnter = function() print("Standing still") end jump.OnEnter = function() print("Jumping!") end jump.OnExit = function() print("Landed") end -- 2. Connect them with transitions. A transition goes in the Transitions list of the state it leaves. table.insert(idle.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Idle", Target = "Walk", Triggers = { "Move" }, })) table.insert(walk.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Walk", Target = "Idle", Triggers = { "StopMoving" }, })) -- One transition can listen for several triggers for _, state in { idle, walk } do table.insert(state.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = state.Name, Target = "Jump", Triggers = { "Jump", "DoubleTap" }, })) end table.insert(jump.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Jump", Target = "Idle", Triggers = { "Land" }, })) -- 3. Create the machine: an ID, the name of the starting state, options, and the states local character = Flux.new("Character", "Idle", nil, { idle, walk, jump }) -- 4. Start it and send triggers character:Start() --> Standing still character:Send("Move") -- Idle -> Walk character:Send("Jump") --> Jumping! character:Send("Move") -- ignored: Jump has no "Move" transition character:Send("Land") --> Landed, Standing still print(character.Current and character.Current.Name) --> Idle   Next, read the Usage guide, the Combat guide, or jump to the API reference.

searchDocs.title: Callback​
searchDocs.content: </> type Callback = ( machine: Machine, ...any ) → () The type of State.OnEnter and State.OnExit. Receives the machine, then any event data.

searchDocs.title: Effect​
searchDocs.content: </> type Effect = ( machine: Machine, ...any ) → () A transition action. Receives the machine, then any event data.

searchDocs.title: Condition​
searchDocs.content: </> type Condition = ( machine: Machine, ...any ) → boolean A transition guard. Receives the machine, then any event data, and returns whether the transition may fire.

searchDocs.title: Details​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Details { Context: C?-- The machine's starting context table. Defaults to {}. DebugMode: boolean?-- Prints every transition, rejected trigger, and how long each callback took HistorySize: number?-- How many state names Machine:GetHistory keeps. Defaults to 8; 0 turns it off. CatchYields: boolean?-- Errors when a callback yields, instead of holding the machine until it resumes. On in DebugMode. See Machine:Send. } The options table passed to Flux.new.

searchDocs.title: Trigger​
searchDocs.content: </> type Trigger = string A trigger name.

searchDocs.title: StateName​
searchDocs.content: </> type StateName = string A state name.

searchDocs.title: UpdateCallback​
searchDocs.content: </> type UpdateCallback = ( machine: Machine, dt: number ) → () The type of State.OnUpdate. Receives the machine and the dt passed to Machine:Update.

searchDocs.title: Resistance​
searchDocs.content: </> type Resistance = number | (machine: Machine) → number The type of [State.Resistance]: a number, or a function that returns one, so it can change over time.

searchDocs.title: RejectReason​
searchDocs.content: </> type RejectReason = "NoTransition" | "Conditions" | "Resisted" | "Inactive" Why a trigger didn't fire a transition, as passed to Machine.Rejected and returned by [Machine:CanSend]: "NoTransition": nothing in the current state, its parents or the machine's AnyTransitions listens for the trigger "Conditions": something listens, but its Conditions failed "Resisted": something listens, but its Priority is below the current state's Resistance "Inactive": the machine isn't running

searchDocs.title: Snapshot​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Snapshot { State: string?-- The current state's name, or nil when the machine isn't running Time: number-- How long the machine has been in it, in machine time } Returned by Machine:Snapshot. Plain data, so it can be sent through a RemoteEvent and applied with Machine:ForceState.

searchDocs.title: Connection​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Connection { Disconnect: (self: Connection) → ()-- Stops the handler from being called } Returned by Signal:Connect.

searchDocs.title: State​
searchDocs.content: </> Flux.State: State The State constructor: Flux.State.new(name).

searchDocs.title: Transition​
searchDocs.content: </> Flux.Transition: Transition The Transition constructor: Flux.Transition.new(params).

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Flux.new( id: any,-- Any value that identifies the machine. Used in error messages. default: string,-- The name of the state entered by Machine:Start details: Details?,-- Options: the machine's Context, DebugMode, HistorySize and CatchYields states: {State}?-- The machine's states ) → Machine Creates a machine. It doesn't enter any state until Machine:Start is called. local player = Flux.new("Player", "Alive", { Context = { Health = 100 } }, { alive, dead }) player:Start() For a typed context, annotate the result: local machine: Flux.Machine<MyContext> = Flux.new(...)

searchDocs.title: States​
searchDocs.content: local state = Flux.State.new("Name")   A State has a Name, a list of Transitions that can leave it, and optional OnEnter and OnExit callbacks. Names must be unique within a machine, because transitions target states by name.  Like every callback, OnEnter and OnExit receive the machine, followed by any event data sent with the trigger.

searchDocs.title: Transitions​
searchDocs.content: Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Locked", Target = "Open", Triggers = { "Unlock" }, Conditions = { function(machine, ...) return hasKey end }, -- optional Effects = { function(machine, ...) playSound("click") end }, -- optional })   A Transition goes in the Transitions list of the state it leaves, and its From must match that state (Start() checks).  When a trigger is sent, the current state checks its transitions in the order they were inserted and fires the first one that listens for that trigger and whose Conditions all pass. If none match, the trigger is ignored.  -- A door that only opens with a key, and stays locked otherwise local hasKey = false table.insert(locked.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Locked", Target = "Open", Triggers = { "Use" }, Conditions = { function() return hasKey end, }, })) door:Send("Use") -- false: condition failed, still Locked hasKey = true door:Send("Use") -- true: now Open

searchDocs.title: The machine​
searchDocs.content: local machine = Flux.new(id, defaultState, details?, states?) machine:Start() machine:Send("Trigger") machine:Stop()   id is any value that identifies the machine in error messages. details takes the machine's Context and a DebugMode flag that prints every transition and how long each callback took. See Flux.new and Machine for everything a machine has.

searchDocs.title: Event data​
searchDocs.content: Anything passed to Send after the trigger name is event data. It's passed, after the machine, to every callback the trigger runs: the Conditions, the old state's OnExit, the Effects, and the new state's OnEnter.  table.insert(alive.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Alive", Target = "Dead", Triggers = { "Hit" }, Conditions = { function(machine, damage) return damage >= machine.Context.Health end, }, })) dead.OnEnter = function(machine, damage, attacker) print(`Killed by {attacker} for {damage} damage`) end player:Send("Hit", 25, "Zombie") -- not enough damage: stays Alive player:Send("Hit", 150, "Boss") --> Killed by Boss for 150 damage   Start() and Stop() pass no event data: the default state's OnEnter and the last state's OnExit receive only the machine.

searchDocs.title: Context​
searchDocs.content: Every machine has a Context table for data its callbacks share, such as health, ammo or a target. Pass the starting table as Context in details, or leave it out to start with an empty table.  local player = Flux.new("Player", "Alive", { Context = { Health = 100, Ammo = 30 } }, { alive, dead }) table.insert(alive.Transitions, Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Alive", Target = "Alive", Triggers = { "Shoot" }, Conditions = { function(machine) return machine.Context.Ammo > 0 end, }, Effects = { function(machine) machine.Context.Ammo -= 1 end, }, })) player:Send("Shoot") print(player.Context.Ammo) --> 29   machine.Context is the same table you passed in, so changes made from outside the machine are visible to its callbacks, and the other way round.

searchDocs.title: Listening for state changes​
searchDocs.content: machine.StateChanged is a signal that fires whenever machine.Current changes. Handlers receive the new state, the old state, then any event data passed to Send.  local connection = player.StateChanged:Connect(function(newState, oldState, damage, attacker) print(oldState and oldState.Name, "->", newState and newState.Name, damage, attacker) end) player:Start() --> nil -> Alive player:Send("Hit", 150, "Boss") --> Alive -> Dead 150 Boss player:Stop() --> Dead -> nil connection:Disconnect()   It fires after the new state's OnEnter, so machine.Current is already the new state.On Start() the old state is nil, and on Stop() the new state is nil. Neither passes event data.A self-transition fires it too, with the same state as both arguments.A Send made from a handler is queued like one made from any other callback.Destroy() disconnects every handler.  Handlers run on their own thread (with task.spawn on Roblox, plain coroutines elsewhere). If a handler yields, the machine may have moved on by the time it resumes, so use the newState argument rather than reading machine.Current after a yield.

searchDocs.title: Transition order​
searchDocs.content: Every transition runs in the same order:  The current state's OnExitThe transition's Effects, in ordermachine.Current is set to the new stateThe new state's OnEntermachine.StateChanged fires  A transition from a state to itself (Target equal to its own name) runs the full exit and enter.

searchDocs.title: Sending triggers from callbacks​
searchDocs.content: You can call Send from inside OnEnter, OnExit, an Effect or a Condition. The trigger, and any event data with it, is queued and runs after the current transition has fully finished, so callbacks never see a half-finished transition. A queued Send returns false, because nothing has transitioned yet when it returns.  loading.OnEnter = function(machine) loadAssets() machine:Send("Loaded") -- runs after Loading has been fully entered end local game = Flux.new("Game", "Loading", nil, { loading, menu }) game:Start() -- Loading -> Menu   If a callback yields (for example with task.wait()), the transition isn't finished until it resumes, so any triggers sent in the meantime are queued too. To wait inside a state, use machine:GetScope():Delay() instead; set CatchYields = true in the details (on in DebugMode) to make an accidental yield an error.  Stop() and Destroy() called from inside a callback also wait until the transition finishes. They then discard any queued triggers.

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: Start() checks the setup. It throws before entering anything if the default state doesn't exist, two states share a name, a transition's Target isn't one of the machine's states or its From doesn't match the state it's in, or a Parent, Initial, Next or Except names a state that doesn't exist. Typos fail at setup instead of mid-game.Errors in callbacks are rethrown from the Send (or Start) that ran them. The machine stays usable afterwards. If the error happened partway through a transition, machine.Current is whatever state the machine had reached: still the old state if an OnExit or Effect threw, or the new state if its OnEnter threw.  For durations, timers, cleanup scopes, interrupts, input buffering, hierarchical states and more, see Combat.

searchDocs.title: Types​
searchDocs.content: Flux is written in --!strict and exports its types from the package: Flux.Machine<C>, Flux.State<C>, Flux.Transition<C>, Flux.Details<C>, Flux.Callback<C>, Flux.Condition<C>, Flux.Effect<C>, Flux.UpdateCallback<C>, Flux.Resistance<C>, Flux.Scope, Flux.Snapshot, Flux.RejectReason, Flux.Trigger and Flux.StateName.  C is the type of the machine's context. It's optional and defaults to any.

searchDocs.title: Typed context​
searchDocs.content: To have machine.Context type-checked, write a type for it and add it to your annotations:  type Combat = { Health: number, Hits: { number } } local alive: Flux.State<Combat> = Flux.State.new("Alive") local dead: Flux.State<Combat> = Flux.State.new("Dead") alive.OnEnter = function(machine) machine.Context.Health = 100 -- checked: Health is a number end local hit: Flux.Transition<Combat> = Flux.Transition.new({ From = "Alive", Target = "Dead", Triggers = { "Hit" }, Effects = { function(machine, damage: number) table.insert(machine.Context.Hits, damage) end, }, }) table.insert(alive.Transitions, hit) local context: Combat = { Health = 100, Hits = {} } local player: Flux.Machine<Combat> = Flux.new("Player", "Alive", { Context = context }, { alive, dead }) player.Context.Helth = 50 -- type error: Combat has no field "Helth"   Event data isn't checked, since it can be anything per trigger. Annotate it in the callback instead, like damage: number above.
